checks: For positive Q at most the total mass, every nonvertical tail is continuous, is the total mass below all fiber supports, and vanishes above them. Its largest threshold with tail at least Q has exact mass Q. The finite pure-base tail has a closed right endpoint, even at a jump. The deepest set on the canonical hull is therefore convex and its projection contains conv(I). Every integer point in that projection is sampled by completeness, so the integer points of conv(I) are exactly I.

For a fixed p and continuous part normalized by the positive definite covariance norm, the terms independent of tilt are uniformly bounded near the mark. Choosing the clipping cutoff strictly outside that bound preserves every sampled trace, including all saturated statuses. At the minimum-norm representative, displacements in either direction in the kernel of the active rows remain feasible for a sufficiently small step. The representative is the pseudoinverse solution for an independent active-row basis with entries bounded by the cutoff. The bound is uniform over finitely many row bases and includes rank zero.

Proper own cuts mean their thresholds lie strictly between the two own support extrema. Compactness of the norm sphere gives a uniform proper neighborhood. The pure-base depth is unchanged at fixed p. Clipping the through-mark tails proves attainment of the nonvertical minimum. Clipping a near-active right quantile preserves both its mass and its own threshold. A proper own section gives strict local decrease, so monotonicity identifies the preserved threshold as the right quantile.

Every omitted quantile term has negative slack separated from zero at y, since all right-quantile inequalities hold there. The variation with the mark is uniformly bounded, independently of tilt. The clipped compact maximum is zero at y and nonnegative nearby by the global depth bound and a proper attaining cap when depth equals Q. The convex maximum rule gives the origin in the convex hull of active gradients u minus ε∇f. Carathéodory in the continuous dimension yields at most d+1 positive weights after removing zeros. Strict own concavity at a midpoint of two deepest marks contradicts the active equality there.

The full affine upper support produces the global lower bound ψ(z,X)≥b·(z−p). The selected quantile inequalities make b·(z−p)≤0 on I and then on its hull. Its zero face contains the minimal face of p. On that face every full fiber has ψ≥0 and every deepest mark has ψ=0. Positive weights force each individual contact equality. A second zero, even on the boundary, contradicts strict own concavity along the open segment from the interior zero. The own gradient vanishes at every such contact.

A relative-interior witness in each maximal occupied face suffices. If two distinct witnesses have the same parity, their integer midpoint is in the relative interior of the smallest face containing both, since every face containing their midpoint contains both endpoints. This contradicts maximality. Parity on I injects into parity on P because an ambient lattice half-difference of two points of I lies in the direction space of aff(I). A nonnegative weighted margin ensures at least one nonnegative individual margin and therefore an actual buffered mass at most Q for each assigned whole-fiber point.

Both source digests match. In 8effe5eb4947ba88 §§1–2, (1)–(2) give the same mass-Q contact menus and maximal occupied-face argument. In 86dd5366456916a8 §4, the clipping and right-quantile mechanism works for any compact continuous-normal normalization sphere, so the use of the covariance sphere here is valid.

The revised raw JSON equals the originally reviewed bytes after one exact deletion in the statement. It removes the sentence referring to a separate small-scale attainment theorem. The proof, the stated own-interiority, proper own-section and pure-base gap hypotheses, every conditional conclusion, and all dependency and source metadata are unchanged. The original exact proof review applies to the revised statement.

The continuation assumes an actual cover of precisely this kind. The revised theorem still supplies fixed finite assigned sets, mass-Q caps with Γ-unit continuous normals, positive probability weights, proper own sections at their individual contacts, nonnegative contact functions with exactly one interior zero at each assigned base, and all deepest bases in I. These provide the old contact minima, proper sections for the cap inverses, and the off-I strict old gap. The continuation does not invoke a small-scale attainment conclusion.
